en: The Ritual for the Repentance of Bhaisajyaguru for Eliminating Calamities and Extending Life, Volume One:
Purifying the Altar for the Practice of the Bhaisajyaguru Repentance Ritual.
With willow branches and pure water, one sprinkles throughout the trichiliocosm. The eight benefits of the nature of emptiness bless humans and devas; merit and wisdom increase and expand.
Sins are extinguished and transgressions removed; the flames are transformed into red lotuses.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śītalabhūmi (three times).
Homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva (three times). (When the assembly has finished reciting the *Mahākaruṇā-hṛdaya-sūtra*, chant: Mahāprajñāpāramitā (and so forth).
Oṃ namo bhagavatyai āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā oṃ sarva-saṃskāra pariśuddha dharmate gagaṇasamudgate svāhā.
Rama-te. Ga-ga-da. Sang-ma-uk-ga-te. Svābhāva. Pi-shu-te. Ma-ha-na-ya. Ba-li-wa-li-svā-hā.
May these supreme merits bring blessings and long life to the Emperor for ten thousand myriad years.
O Sage and Enlightened Ruler, may the kings of all nations come to pay court. Namo Amitāyus. May there be blessings and praise.
Long live the Emperor ten thousand times ten thousand years! (Repeat.

By the merit and power of this scripture and its dhāraṇī, we dedicate it to the Dharma-protecting dragons, devas, and the numinous intelligences of the Three Realms, mountains, and rivers, as well as to the true masters who guard this site of practice.
Praying for blessings and the security of peace and goodness;
may all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm together enter the nature-ocean of Vairocana.
(Incense Praise)
As the incense in the burner is first ignited, the entire Dharma realm is perfumed; the assembly of Bhaiṣajyaguru deities hears it from afar, gathering auspicious clouds wherever they dwell.
As one’s sincere devotion grows ever more earnest, all Buddhas manifest their complete bodies.
Gandhamegha-canopied Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva (Recite three times; kneel and recite one scroll of the *Bhaiṣajyaguru-sūtra*).
Universal-Worthy-King Bodhisattva: A Bodhisattva arrives in an elephant carriage, seated in the full lotus posture, named Universal-Worthy.
His body is the color of white jade, emitting fifty kinds of light; these fifty kinds of light form a halo around his neck.
From all the pores of his body, golden light flows forth, and at the tips of this golden light, there are immeasurable transformation Buddhas and various transformed Bodhisattvas.
Taking them as their retinue, they walk slowly and with composed grace; great jeweled flowers rain down before the practitioner.
The elephant opens its mouth, and from the various ponds upon its tusks, jade maidens play music and sing, their voices exquisitely subtle and wondrous.
Praising the Mahāyāna, the Way of Single Reality, the practitioner, having seen it,
rejoices and pays homage; furthermore, they read and recite the extremely profound sūtras,
universally pay homage to the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions, and pay homage to the stūpa of the Buddha Prabhūtaratna.
And to Śākyamuni, as well as to Samantabhadra— bowing to all these great Bodhisattvas,
I make this vow: "If by my past merit I am destined to see Samantabhadra,
may the Honored One, Samantabhadra, manifest his physical body to me."
Samantabhadra-rāja Bodhisattva Mahāsattva (three times):
With all respect and single-minded devotion, I prostrate at the feet of the eternally abiding Buddhas of the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm.

With single-minded devotion, they prostrate to the eternally abiding Dharma of the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm; with single-minded devotion, they prostrate to the eternally abiding Sangha of the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm.
Each of these assemblies knelt upon their right knees and, holding incense and flowers, made offerings according to the Dharma.
May these incense and flowers pervade the ten directions, Becoming subtle and wondrous towers of light;
With celestial music and divine precious incense, Celestial delicacies and divine precious robes—
Inconceivable particles of the sublime Dharma, From each single particle, may all particles emerge.
From every single atom emerge all dharmas, revolving without obstruction and mutually adorning one another;

they reach before the Triple Gem in the ten directions. Before the Triple Gem throughout the dharma-realm of the ten directions, my own body appears in each place to perform offerings, and each of these bodies pervades the entire dharma-realm.
In each and every place, without confusion or obstruction, they perform the work of Buddhas throughout the bounds of the future;
universally perfuming all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, those who receive this perfuming all resolve their minds on Bodhi and together enter the non-arising realization of Buddha-wisdom.
May these clouds of incense and flowers pervade the worlds of the ten directions, making offerings to all Buddhas,
the Honored Dharma, and the Bodhisattvas, as well as the assembly of Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas,
and all devas and ṛṣis. May they arise as platforms of radiant light, extending beyond boundless realms throughout infinite Buddha-fields.
Performing Buddha-work through his reception, he universally perfumes all sentient beings; All have resolved their minds on Bodhi.
His countenance is most wondrous and sublime, And his radiance illuminates the ten directions.
I have previously made offerings to him, And now I come again to behold him in person—the Holy Lord, King among Gods, With a voice like that of the kalaviṅka bird.
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, we now pay homage.
*Namo* to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ratnakusuma. (Recite three times.
Medicine Master Tathāgata, please bear witness to this rite of repentance. (The presiding master recites the verses of harmony and makes the formal announcement.)
Delusive thoughts give rise to birth and death; True Suchness is unchanging and does not transmigrate. This Dharani is inconceivable.

Without abiding, I proclaim it in the presence of emptiness, reverently looking up to the Triple Gem of the ten directions, Bhaisajyaguru Tathagata, the devas and nagas of the lands and seas, and all the assembly of holy ones. I pray that you will grant [your blessings].
O Compassionate One, deign to grant your witness and scrutiny. This memorial is hereby proclaimed; we humbly entreat you to listen with attentive ear.
(Having finished the proclamation of the intent:
The foregoing sentiments have been reverently proclaimed before you. Within the Great Perfect Mirror, we trust you will grant your seal of approval. For this reason, incense is offered.
We offer flowers as an act of worship and adorn the altar with lamps and candles. We request that you, our honored predecessors, perform the ritual of repentance on our behalf.

Now, relying upon the Tathāgata’s Great Ocean of Quiescent Extinction and taking refuge in the King of Vows of Universal Gate and Great Compassion, we shall wash away our karmic offenses in the realm of non-existence and prune away the thorns of affliction from the ground where sprouts have not yet emerged.
Our minds shall be purely Dharma, in accord with the Dharma, and in harmony with its principle.
The affairs are perfectly harmonized; vows and practices are fulfilled. Since I am thus, the Buddha will surely take pity on me. I pray to Your vast compassion for secret influence and empowerment.
The Buddha’s face is like the pure full moon, and also like a thousand suns radiating brilliant light.
The circular halo shines universally throughout the ten directions; Joy, renunciation, compassion, and kindness are all fully perfected.
In this Ritual of Repentance for the Avalambana of the Medicine Master’s Path of Awakened Activity, we now take refuge in the Buddhas of the three periods.
Namo to the past Buddha Vipaśyin. Namo to the Buddha Śikhin.
Homage to Vipaśyin Buddha; homage to Śikhin Buddha; homage to Viśvabhū Buddha;
homage to Krakucchanda Buddha; homage to Kanakamuni Buddha; homage to Kāśyapa Buddha;
homage to our Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha; homage to the future Honored One Maitreya Buddha.
Homage to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha.
Homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Ocean-like Assembly of Bhaiṣajyaguru. (Recite three times.
Verse for Opening the Sutra:
The unsurpassed, most profound, and subtle Dharma, Difficult to encounter in hundreds of thousands of myriads of kalpas— I have now seen, heard, and received it;
may I uphold it. I pray that you will explain the meaning of the Tathāgata’s Method of Repentance.
*The Ritual for the Medicine Master Buddha to Eliminate Calamities and Prolong Life*, Volume One.
All Buddhas, out of compassion for sentient beings, have expounded the *Bhaiṣajyaguru* Dharma-Assembly Repentance Method.

This is because sentient beings possess heavy defilements, are shrouded by the darkness of ignorance, are unacquainted with cause and effect, and do not diligently practice repentance. They indulge in greed, anger, and delusion, and give free rein to killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct.
Their committed sins and impurities are immeasurable and boundless; the karmic enmities they have contracted are likewise immeasurable and boundless, yet they remain unaware of them.

Unaware of this, [their transgressions] grow deeper and thicker day by day, leading them to shorten their natural lifespans and meet with untimely death; to be dismissed from their official positions and sink into lowliness;

to have their wealth and abundance stripped away and fall into poverty; to see their children and wives perish and be left alone; thus they encounter these nine types of violent deaths and fall into the three miserable realms.

The various bitter fruits of suffering are self-inflicted and self-received; these manifold retributions for evil deeds manifest either in the present or in the future, without the slightest deviation.
Whether delayed or immediate, the retribution must surely follow. At that time...

The Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha, out of compassion and for the sake of salvation, has preached this *Sūtra on the Merits of His Original Vows*, so that those who read and recite it shall fashion seven images of that Tathāgata. Before each image, one shall place seven lamps;
the size of each lamp shall be as large as a chariot wheel, and they shall be kept burning for forty-nine days without the light being extinguished. This applies specifically to the Kṣatriya caste.
"O great layperson, you possess abundant wealth and treasures, with granaries and storehouses overflowing; you are well-suited for this task.
Yet, there are sentient beings of meager strength who, though their hearts may rejoice, are unable to perform the ritual adornments according to the Dharma.

For this reason, I have translated from the *Benyuan Gongde Jing* (Sutra of Original Vows and Merit) the *Xiaozai Yanshou Chanfa* (Repentance Rite for Eliminating Calamities and Extending Life), so that all sentient beings may observe the fasts and precepts, bathe themselves, or..."

Whether in a monastery or at home, whether inviting fellow practitioners of meditation or associating with virtuous friends, one should sweep and cleanse the site, perform incense offerings and cultivation, provide offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, and candles according to one's means, chant praises according to the ritual manuals, and pay reverent homage with sincere devotion; then there will be no request that is not granted.
There is no vow that is not fulfilled. As the Sūtra says: "To confess past transgressions is what the Pure Name (Vimalakīrti) esteems.

To reform the past and cultivate the future, to wash the body and mind clean, to sever all evils, and to vow never to create them again—thus the offenses of many kalpas are purified until nothing remains.
Whatever one seeks and desires shall be entirely satisfied. We [the practitioners] prostrate with a sincere heart, seeking mercy and repenting.

Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, one next performs repentance. Contemplating the time when the Semblance Dharma (*pratirūpaka-dharma*) prevails, if there are sentient beings who, desiring to benefit and bring peace and happiness to others, seek to eliminate all karmic obstructions and establish supreme merit;

or those who, desiring to fulfill the great vows of all Buddhas, fully uphold the names of all Buddhas and the precious treasury of the True Dharma (*saddharma-ratnakośa*); or those who [desire]— [Note: The provided source text appears to be incomplete at the end.]
Having attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, with their bodies adorned by the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics,
those who desire to obtain immeasurable wisdom and skillful means (*upāya*) in order to establish all sentient beings in the Mahāyāna— [should practice this].

Desiring to practice the holy life (*brahmacarya*), they wish to attain unimpaired precepts, to be endowed with the three clusters of morality (*trisaṃvaraśīla*), and to be ultimately pure without any transgression.
Desiring to have all their faculties complete and free from the suffering of disease, and for their family members and requisites to be entirely abundant, they wish to break the snare-net of Māra,
to be liberated from the entanglements of all non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*), and to uproot various evils.
Regarding those who see the dense forest: if there is a woman who wishes to transform her female state into that of a man and possess the marks of a man;
or one who, desiring sons or daughters, obtains sons or daughters; or one who, seeking long life, obtains long life;

or one who is subject to royal law and desires liberation from all sorrow and suffering; or one who desires to obtain exquisite food and drink and be satiated with the flavor of the Dharma—and so forth.

Regarding various superior and exquisite garments and all manner of precious ornaments, he desires to practice generosity, being entirely free from greed or attachment toward whatever he possesses as he bestows them upon those who come seeking.

He desires to attain right view and diligence, to well-discipline his intentions, to become learned and sharp-witted, to understand the most profound meanings, to constantly seek the supreme Dharma, and to always encounter virtuous friends; thus, he desires to receive, uphold, and study [the teachings].

May those who dwell here and aspire to be born in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, in the presence of Amitāyus Buddha, to hear and study the True Dharma—should they have broken precepts and wish to restore them to purity; should their lives be exhausted and wish to have them prolonged;
or should they wish to eliminate, subdue, and cause to vanish all manner of calamities and various hardships for their nations and the masses—may [their wishes be fulfilled].

At that time, those who seek joy should adorn themselves in accordance with the Dharma and take refuge in the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha. With single-minded diligence, they should cultivate *samādhi*. Why is this?
Because when that Tathāgata was practicing the bodhisattva path, he made twelve subtle and sublime supreme vows, and through their extraordinary merit, he [brought about these results].
All who hear this shall have their karmic obstructions eliminated and all their aspirations fulfilled.

Therefore, those bodhisattvas bound to only one more birth who are able to believe and understand it as it truly is and practice according to what is taught, should [offer] their very body, life, and wealth.
Without giving rise to stinginess or regret, exert all one's strength in adornment, and one will certainly attain fulfillment.
Therefore, on this day, together with the assembly present before us, each should with a sincere heart take refuge and pay homage.

Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, I take refuge with a sincere heart. I pray that all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will equally exercise their compassion and descend upon this ritual site.
May all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, as well as the yakṣa generals, give rise to pity and come to this ritual site.
May all these noble assemblies bear witness: today, I desire to cultivate unexcelled Bodhi for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions and the six realms of existence.
I shall sever all karmic obstructions and enter together with them into the ocean of the Tathāgata’s original great vows.
Manifesting form-bodies everywhere, within a single thought-moment, I shall make offerings to all the Triple Gem of the ten directions. In one...
Within this mindfulness, I universally deliver all sentient beings of the six realms, causing them to enter the great wisdom of equality.
Therefore, on this day, I shall practice with single-minded diligence according to the teachings. I only pray that all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas [will grant their protection].

By the power of the original vows of Bhaisajyaguru Tathāgata, may he accept my repentance and cause all that I practice to definitively destroy my karmic obstacles, so that my conduct and vows may be fully perfected. As described in the sutra, may you grant your witness to all of this.
*Namo* to the Tathāgata Bhaisajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, vast in radiance, sublime in merit, and whose body...
They dwell securely. Adorned with nets of flames, they surpass the sun and moon; all sentient beings in the darkness receive illumination and awakening.
Whatever they seek according to their inclinations is entirely fulfilled. All sickness and suffering are completely extinguished.
Immeasurable bodhisattvas practice immeasurable skillful means and immeasurable vast vows. If I were to spend an eon, or even more than an eon...
To speak extensively: though an eon may swiftly come to an end, the vows and practices of that Buddha, along with his skillful means, are inexhaustible.
Therefore, with a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to him with my head bowed.
Namo bhagavate vīrasena kuru-vaiḍūrya-prabha-rājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya. Tadyathā. Oṃ.
Vikṣate, vikṣate, vikṣa-sa, samudgate svāhā. Praise to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru.
His world is of lapis lazuli; his kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity accord with all that is appropriate. Through this method of repentance, he delivers the masses from delusion.
I prostrate and take refuge. May all my aspirations and requests be fulfilled.
Medicine Master Buddha, Medicine Master Buddha, Medicine Master Buddha who Eliminates Calamities and Extends Life.
Namo Medicine Master Buddha who Eliminates Calamities and Extends Life.
(Circumambulate the altar, recite the verses of praise for the Buddha, and dedicate the merit through mindfulness of the Buddha.
I bow my head to the World-Honored One, the Medicine Master, the Perfectly Awakened One in the Realm of the Full Moon in the East;
he who has fulfilled the fruits of three great eons, inconceivable and marvelous, whose ten titles and renown are peerless.
The twenty-six gates of vows are initiated on the ground of practice; The hundreds of thousands of marks and signs are perfected within the fruition.
The ocean of compassion is vast and difficult to fathom; The mountain of merit is high and beyond full praise.
Namo to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha of the Eastern Pure Vaidūrya World.
Homage to the Medicine Master Buddha who Eliminates Calamities and Extends Life (Recite one hundred or one thousand times as desired, then dedicate the merit).

Lord of Compassion within the trichiliocosm, Great Dharma King of the ten billion continents, I pray you open your lotus eyes to behold the sentiments of ordinary beings; Whatever the sentient beings seek, all shall be answered.
All Buddhas, out of compassion for sentient beings, have expounded the Medicine Master’s Ritual of Repentance for the Bodhimanda. Now we take refuge.

Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, we next perform repentance. [Disciple] So-and-so and others, on behalf of the four debts of gratitude, the three realms of existence, and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, universally vow to sever and eliminate the three obstacles. We take refuge and repent: I and all sentient beings...

From the beginning until now, due to craving and false views, you have internally conceived of a self and persons, and externally relied upon evil friends. You did not rejoice in even a hair’s breadth of another’s merit;

instead, you pervaded your three karmas with nothing but the commission of manifold sins. Although the acts themselves were not numerous, your evil intent was widespread, continuing day and night without interruption.
You concealed and denied your transgressions, desiring that others not know of them, and felt no fear of the evil realms. There was none—

Lacking a sense of shame and dread of blame, I denied cause and effect. For such karmic obstacles, having not yet undergone repentance, I now, before the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru, deeply believe in cause and effect, give rise to profound shame and dread, and feel great fear.

I openly confess and repent, severing the continuity of these thoughts, vowing to attain Bodhicitta, abandoning evil and cultivating good, diligently exerting my three karmas, and turning [from them].
I now repent of my past transgressions. I rejoice in even a hair’s breadth of merit belonging to all ordinary beings and sages alike.

I take refuge in the Buddha Bhaiṣajyaguru, whose great power of vows is able to rescue and deliver me, enabling me to emerge from the sea of the two deaths and reach the shore of the three virtues. I pray that you will look upon me with compassion and pity, and grant me your protection.
Each of us, with a sincere heart, takes refuge and pays homage.

Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, we next perform repentance. We, the disciples [Name] and others, from beginningless time until this very day, have suffered from the diseases of greed, anger, and jealousy;
the diseases of arrogance and self-conceit; the disease of failing to distinguish between good and evil;
the disease of lacking faith in the retribution of sin and merit; the disease of committing the five heinous acts of unfiliality; and the disease of bringing disgrace and ruin upon the Triple Gem.
The disease of not practicing the fast and precepts; the disease of violating the *śīla*; the disease of praising oneself and disparaging others; the disease of insatiable greed for gain;
the disease of being deluded by sounds and pursuing forms; the disease of craving scents and attachment to tactile sensations; the disease of believing in heterodox and inverted views;
the disease of indulging in lust and addiction to alcohol, as well as unrestrained and excessive negligence; even if one were to encounter a physician, they would administer the wrong medicine.
Regarding these illnesses, as well as the afflictions of calamities and insults beyond measure, and the maladies of physical and mental suffering caused by the torment of grief and sorrow—
should one wish for such sufferings to be eliminated and all sought-after aspirations to be fulfilled,
at that time the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha enters a samādhi called "The Elimination of All Suffering of Sentient Beings."
Having entered meditative absorption, he emitted a great radiance from within his uṣṇīṣa.
Within that light, he proclaimed this great dhāraṇī: Namo bhagavate viśvāmitra-vaidūryaprabhāsa-rājāya.
Tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya. Tadyathā: Oṃ viśve viśve viśva-samudgate svāhā.
At that time, after this mantra had been spoken within the light, the great earth shook, and a vast radiance was emitted. All sentient beings...
All the sufferings of illness are eliminated, and one experiences peaceful and secure bliss. Thus we know that the merit of repentance is the spiritual panacea that heals all maladies of the mind;
it is the wondrous prescription for understanding life and attaining liberation from death.
Great Physician-King, you prescribe medicine according to the disease: namely, loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity are the medicine;
patience and gentleness are the medicine; right faith in the Triple Gem is the medicine; diligent cultivation of merit and wisdom is the medicine; the six pāramitās are the medicine;

fully partaking of the nectar of immortality is the medicine; greedily seeking the flavor of the Dharma is the medicine; cultivating the truth and nourishing the vital energy is the medicine; returning to the source and restoring the origin is the medicine.
The original is medicine. To be able to reform one’s transgressions is medicine. Skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) is medicine. To remain unmoved in voice or countenance is medicine.
To purify the mind and sever desire is medicine. One should constantly take such medicines as these, having pounded, sifted, and compounded them, and ingest them at the proper time.
If sentient beings are ill, they should all suffer from the same illness; if sentient beings require medicine, they should all receive the same medicine. If [the Buddha] were to speak extensively...
These phenomena are called "inversions. If one speaks according to the true reality (*dharmatā*) of the One Vehicle, then what is increased and what is decreased?
What is defiled and what is pure? What is good and what is evil? What is sin and what is merit? What is sickness and what is medicine?

Contemplating past expedient means is like a person in a dream who dreams that his body has fallen ill; he seeks a physician and takes medicine until he is cured. Yet, upon waking from the dream, he realizes [it was all empty].

Originally there is no illness; even "no illness" does not exist, let alone medicine. Therefore, the illnesses of sentient beings are one and the same as illusory illnesses, and the medicines of the Tathāgata are one and the same as illusory medicines.

Thus we know that the Dharma taught by the Tathāgata has but a single characteristic and a single flavor—namely, the characteristic of liberation, the characteristic of detachment, and the characteristic of cessation—which is ultimate *nirvāṇa* and ultimately returns to emptiness, just like [the moisture from] a single cloud.

It rained, and the medicinal trees, both large and small, each attained lush growth. We, now having received the power of the Buddha’s grace, have heard the name of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha. No longer shall we face the hardships of illness and suffering;
rather, we shall be able to ultimately attain unsurpassed bodhi. Therefore, today we have gathered together, all with one mind.
Until the end of this life, I take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.
Now I shall take refuge in all Buddhas: Namo Vairocana Buddha; Namo our Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha;
Namo Bhaisajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabhāsa Tathāgata; Namo Amitāyus Buddha.
Homage to all Buddhas of the past throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm;
homage to all Buddhas of the present throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm;
homage to all Buddhas of the future throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm.
Homage to the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha, and his Merit of Original Vows Sūtra.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryavairocana. Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Candravairocana.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. Homage to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta; homage to the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati;
homage to the Bodhisattva Ratnakusuma; homage to the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja;
homage to the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata; homage to the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Dispeller of Calamities and Obstacles; homage to the Bodhisattva Increaser of Merit and Longevity;
homage to the thirty-six thousand bodhisattvas beneath the Tree of Melodious Sound;
homage to the Venerable Ānanda and the eight thousand bhikṣus, the great assembly of noble saṃgha.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Jue (Savior-Deliverer).

Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, one next performs repentance. If there are sentient beings who wish to be delivered from the suffering of illness, one should, for their sake, observe the eightfold precepts (*aṣṭāṅga-śīla*) for seven days and seven nights. One should provide them with food, drink, and other necessary requisites according to one’s ability.

Having prepared these offerings, they shall make offerings to the community of bhikṣus; for six periods of the day and night, they shall perform prostrations and circumambulations, making offerings to that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha, reciting this honored sūtra forty-nine times and lighting forty-nine lamps.
Up until the forty-ninth day, the light shall not cease. Thus, one may transcend the perils of danger and distress, and shall not be seized by various malevolent spirits.
For this reason, today, together with the assembly present before me, each of you should exert yourselves with diligence:

burn incense, scatter flowers, light lamps, and create banners; release living beings and cultivate merit, so that they may be delivered from suffering and calamity and encounter no further hardships. May it be so.
We pray that the Tathāgata will bear witness to our repentance. From beginningless time until this very day, whatever we have done has not accorded with our wishes;
we should know that all of this is the result of the lingering retribution for evil karma from the past.
Therefore, we now earnestly seek repentance, repenting for the evil dreams, ill omens, and various inauspicious signs encountered in the human world.
Repentance for the retribution of malignant diseases among humans that persist for years and months without healing, leaving one bedridden and unable to rise or move;
repentance for the retribution of winter plagues and summer epidemics among humans, such as virulent miasmas and contagious fevers;
repentance for the retribution of water, fire, bandits, and the perils of war among humans; repentance for being seized by lions among humans...
I repent for the retribution of being harmed by cubs, tigers, wolves, venomous snakes, malevolent scorpions, centipedes, and millipedes;

I repent for the retribution of the birth, aging, sickness, and death, as well as the sorrows and afflictions experienced among humans; I repent for the retribution of sentient beings' various evil karmas of body, speech, and mind, which they have created and increased;
I repent for the retribution of sentient beings who are destined to fall into the three evil realms for immeasurable thousands [of kalpas].
I repent for sentient beings’ retribution of enduring various intense sufferings throughout their lifetimes.

I repent for sentient beings’ retribution of wandering endlessly through the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts. I repent for sentient beings’ retribution of being reborn no longer in any other evil destinies.
I repent for sentient beings’ retribution of becoming slaves or servants, subjected to the驱使 (driving and service) of others. I repent for sentient beings who may become oxen...
The retribution for being constantly whipped and beaten as a horse, donkey, or mule; the retribution for being oppressed by hunger and thirst while constantly carrying heavy loads along the road;

and the retribution for practicing human enchantments, *gūdu* poisons, flying corpses (*fei shi*), and malevolent ghosts, falsely creating strange and demonic phenomena—through such means, one shall experience immeasurable calamities, crosswise misfortunes, pestilence, death, and decline among humans and devas in the present and the future.

The retribution for affliction. (The assembly: Today, with utmost sincerity, we turn toward the Buddha Bhaiṣajyaguru and the holy assembly gathered like an ocean, seeking compassion and repenting so that [all faults] may be extinguished.
The preceding section on "the disease and the medicine" has been concluded; both are equally one illusion.
Caused by evil karma, all karmic obstacles shall now be addressed in sequence. We, [Name] and others, vow that through this repentance...
All merits arising from the three obstacles are entirely dedicated and bestowed upon all sentient beings. Together with them, we perform repentance.

We vow that from this day forth until the attainment of Bodhi, all sentient beings shall contemplate the suffering of birth and death, give rise to the Bodhicitta, reform their evils and cultivate goodness, turn away from the heterodox and return to the orthodox, and enjoy peace and happiness of body and mind, with inexhaustible wisdom and an abundance of clothing and food.
Abundant in wealth and resources, with storehouses overflowing; possessing a handsome and upright appearance, they are intelligent, wise, courageous, and majestic.
Protected by various generals and supported by the Buddhas and sages, all their undertakings are entirely auspicious.

Under the compassionate shade [of the Buddha], we disciples, [Name] and others, further pray that from this day forward, we may swiftly realize Bodhi, adorned with the most sublime marks and radiant light.
We pray that all sentient beings, having been enlightened by this light, may proceed wherever they wish and accomplish all their undertakings.
May all sentient beings attain the inexhaustible, so that the objects they enjoy shall never be lacking.
May all sentient beings establish themselves in the Mahāyāna, causing them all to dwell securely within the path to Bodhi. May all sentient beings attain the precepts without deficiency.
Should there be any transgressions or violations, may they be restored to purity. May all sentient beings be upright and possess wisdom;
may their faculties be complete and free from all illness and suffering. May all the ailments of sentient beings be entirely eliminated, and may their families and provisions be fully abundant.
May all sentient beings transform their female bodies into male ones and possess the marks of a great man until they reach enlightenment.
May all sentient beings escape the net of Māra and be liberated from the entanglements of all non-Buddhist paths. May all sentient beings be protected by the laws of the king.

May all those tormented by grief and sorrow attain liberation. May all sentient beings be fully satiated with food and drink, and thereafter find ultimate peace and happiness through the flavor of the Dharma.
May all sentient beings obtain various garments according to their preferences, fulfilling their hearts' desires.
May all sentient beings be long-lived and wealthy; may their official ranks, sons, and daughters, and whatever they seek, all be fulfilled.
May all worlds be freed from the hundred anomalies, the nine untimely deaths, the eight difficulties, and the three calamities, as well as foreign invasions, disturbances, bandits, and rebellions.
All evils and hardships shall be entirely extinguished. The realm shall be peaceful and secure; wind and rain shall follow their proper seasons; crops shall ripen in abundance;
and all sentient beings shall be free from illness and live in joy. Their vows for the practice of bodhi shall increase and become clearer with every thought-moment as they rescue suffering beings.

May they always regard others as themselves. Furthermore, may they, in birth after birth and from lifetime to lifetime, in every place and at every turn, never fall into the remote frontiers, but be born into families of right faith;
may they possess dignified and handsome features, wisdom, and eloquence; may they remain far removed from unwholesome dharmas and draw near to virtuous friends;

may they firmly uphold the practice of the precepts and establish themselves in the Mahāyāna. Moreover, may they, in birth after birth and from lifetime to lifetime, in every place and at every turn, cause the Buddha-dharma to flourish and manifest.
Having shattered the nets of all Māras, they have exerted their resolve to fully cultivate the six pāramitās, extensively practiced offerings, and adorned themselves with merit and wisdom.
Through patience and diligence, they have realized the path to Bodhi. On this day, we ought to remember and repay their kindness.
The grace and virtue of the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha should always thus benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
Therefore, with a sincere heart, we take refuge in him and pay homage to him with our heads bowed.
Namo bhagavate viśva-ūrū-vaiḍūrya-prabha-rāja-tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya. Tadyathā. Oṃ.
Vikṣate, vikṣate, vikṣa-sa, trimukhade svāhā!

Seated upright in the eastern direction, the Unsurpassed King of Physicians possesses twelve great vows that are wondrous and immeasurable; he extinguishes transgressions and eliminates all calamities and misfortunes.
May blessings descend and auspiciousness be bestowed. May your lifespan be increased and made long-lasting.
Medicine Master Buddha, Medicine Master Buddha, Medicine Master Buddha who Eliminates Calamities and Extends Life.

Namo Medicine Master Buddha who Eliminates Calamities and Extends Life. (As before, recite the verse for arising from meditation, circumambulate the altar, recite the Buddha’s name, and perform the dedication.)
The Ritual of Repentance for the Medicine Master Buddha for Eliminating Calamities and Extending Life, Middle Scroll.
The Ritual of Repentance for the Medicine Master Buddha for Eliminating Calamities and Extending Life, Lower Scroll.
The Buddha’s body fills the Dharma-realm, universally appearing before all sentient beings.

Responding to conditions and meeting with sentient beings without exception, yet ever remaining upon this seat of Bodhi—may the Buddhas of the three periods of time, out of compassion for all living beings, preach the Dharma-assembly Repentance Ritual of the Medicine Master. Now we take refuge.
To all Buddhas: Homage to Vairocana Buddha; homage to our Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha;
homage to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha; homage to Amitāyus Buddha.
Homage to all Buddhas of the past throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma realm.
Homage to all Buddhas of the present throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma realm.
Homage to all Buddhas of the future throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma realm.
Homage to the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha, and his Merit of Original Vows Sūtra.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryavairocana. Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Candravairocana.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. Homage to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta; homage to the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati;
homage to the Bodhisattva Ratnakusuma; homage to the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja;
homage to the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata; homage to the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Eliminator of Calamities and Obstacles. Homage to the Bodhisattva Increaser of Merit and Longevity.
Homage to the thirty-six thousand bodhisattvas beneath the Tree of Joyful Sound.
Homage to the Venerable Ānanda and the eight thousand bhikṣus, the great assembly of noble saṃghas.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Jue-duo (Saṃtrāsa).

Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, we next perform repentance. We, the disciples [Name] and others, having already performed repentance as above, should now give rise to a mind free from defilement and turbidity, a mind free from anger and malice, and toward all sentient beings, arouse a heart of benefit, peace, compassion, and loving-kindness.

With a mind of joyful relinquishment and equanimity, he then collects his thoughts and practices right contemplation. He does not sever the fetters and latent tendencies, nor does he dwell within the ocean of those tendencies.
He contemplates all phenomena as empty, according to their true mark. What is meant by "contemplating all phenomena as empty"? The practitioner observes with discernment:
Now, with a single-minded focus: this deluded mind arises following its objects of perception. Is this mind caused by a [prior] mind? Is it not caused by a mind?
Is it both caused and not caused by a mind? Is it neither caused nor not caused by a mind?
Does it exist within the three periods of time? Does it exist internally, externally, or in between? What trace does it leave? Where does it abide?
Within such various causes and conditions as location and so forth, the mind is ultimately unfindable; it is like a dream and like an illusion, without name and without mark.
At that time, the practitioner does not even perceive the mind as saṃsāra, much less perceive the mind as nirvāṇa.
Having obtained neither the object of observation nor the subject of observation, they neither grasp nor reject, neither relying upon nor clinging to anything.
Nor does it abide in quiescence. It transcends the path of language and cannot be expressed. When one contemplates that the mind is no-mind, then sin and merit have no master.
Since the nature of sin and merit is empty, all dharmas are empty. The mind has no object of mind; dharmas do not abide in dharmas.
To perform this repentance is called the Great Repentance; it is called the Repentance that Destroys Consciousness.
By these causes and conditions, the mind becomes tranquil and extinguished in every thought-moment, abiding nowhere, like the great void. Even the void cannot be apprehended;
ultimately it cannot be apprehended, and yet it cannot be apprehended. Spontaneously transcending all samādhis, its radiance shines forth, and the myriad dharmas manifest.
Pervasive and unimpeded, as vast as the *dharmatā* and ultimate as space; may we obtain that which we have prayed for and fulfill our bodhicitta vows.
May the assembly each direct their minds toward this, taking refuge and prostrating with the crown of the head.
Homage to Vairocana Buddha. Homage to our Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha.
Homage to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha. Homage to Amitāyus Buddha.
Homage to all Buddhas of the past throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm.
Homage to all Buddhas of the present, throughout the ten directions and pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
Homage to all Buddhas of the future, throughout the ten directions and pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
Homage to the *Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-tathāgata-praṇidhāna-guṇa-sūtra*.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Sunlight Pervading Illumination; homage to the Bodhisattva Moonlight Pervading Illumination;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī; homage to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta; homage to the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Ratnakusuma; homage to the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja;
homage to the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata; homage to the Bodhisattva Maitreya;
homage to the Bodhisattva Āpadāntakara; homage to the Bodhisattva Puṇyāyuṣyavardhana.
Homage to the thirty-six thousand bodhisattvas beneath the Tree of Delightful Sound.
Homage to the Venerable Ānanda and the eight thousand bhikṣus, the great assembly of noble saṃghas.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Jie-duo (Tārā).
Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, one should next contemplate the true mark of the mind. At every moment and in every action—
whether walking or sitting, entering or exiting, attending to the calls of nature, sweeping or washing, moving about or lifting objects, looking, bowing, or listening—
one should maintain single-mindedness and keep this mindfulness present.

The Three Jewels. Contemplate the emptiness of the nature of the mind. For even a single moment, do not recall the five desires or worldly affairs, nor give rise to thoughts of deviant views, engage in conversation or debate with outsiders, indulge in negligence or frivolous laughter, gaze at forms or listen to sounds, become attached to various sensory objects, or initiate unwholesome karma, neutral afflictions, or discursive thoughts.
If you are unable to practice in accordance with the Dharma, [the fruit will not be attained]. If indeed...
With mind following upon mind, never departing from the true mark (*dharmatā*), and not sparing even body or life, one practices the method of repentance for the sake of all sentient beings;

this is called "reality. With single-minded diligence, one adorns oneself with the Dharma. Therefore, may the assembly once again, with utmost sincerity, prostrate themselves with their five limbs touching the ground and take refuge, paying homage with the crown of the head.
Ever-abiding Triple Gem.
Homage to Vairocana Buddha. Homage to our Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha.
Homage to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha. Homage to Amitāyus Buddha.
Homage to all Buddhas of the past throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm;
homage to all Buddhas of the present throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm;
homage to all Buddhas of the future throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm.
Homage to the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha, and his Merit of Fundamental Vows;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryavairocana; homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Candravairocana;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī; homage to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta; homage to the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati;
homage to the Bodhisattva Ratnapadmaśrī; homage to the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja;
homage to the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata; homage to the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Dispeller of Calamities and Obstacles; homage to the Bodhisattva Increaser of Merit and Longevity;
homage to the thirty-six thousand bodhisattvas beneath the Tree of Joyful Sound;
homage to the Venerable Ānanda and the eight thousand bhikṣus, the great assembly of noble saṃgha.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Jue (Jude).
Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, we, the disciples [Name] and others, together with all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, from time immemorial have been entangled by the three obstructions.
Because our minds are shrouded and obscured, we have falsely given rise to craving and attachment toward various sensory objects and conditions. We are ignorant...

Deluded and lacking wisdom, deficient in the faculty of faith, they create various kinds of karma through body, speech, and mind, even to the point of disparaging and slandering the True Dharma and violating the precepts (śīla).
They constantly engage in mutually harmful actions. Or, though dwelling in a pure stage, their noble fruition remains incomplete;
as subtle [defilements] continue to flow, it is difficult for them to achieve samādhi. Now, having encountered...

Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabhā Tathāgata, you who swiftly eliminate karmic obstructions and cause one to attain wondrous enlightenment—I therefore turn toward you with a sincere heart, prostrating my forehead in utmost devotion. I confess all my transgressions and beg for repentance.
I pray that your ocean of great compassion will impartially embrace and sustain me, so that for myself and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, past obstructions may naturally...

They are freed from all hardships and liberated; they shatter the shell of ignorance and dry up the river of afflictions. With right view, they attain awakening; their wondrous mind becomes clear and penetrating.

They dwell securely in bodhi, with constant radiance manifest before them. Free from illness, they enjoy peace and happiness. All adornments as they desire and seek are fully provided according to their hearts' wishes.
Their faculties are sharp and keen; they are learned and possess thorough understanding. They maintain the holy life with diligence and enter into samādhi.
By means of immeasurable and boundless wisdom and skillful means, they cause all sentient beings to obtain the necessities of life without any lack,
to skillfully cultivate the various practices of a bodhisattva, and to swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. When the time approaches for their final passing,
they will be clear-minded and at ease, certain of proceeding to the West, to the World of Ultimate Bliss of Amitāyus Buddha.
The eight great bodhisattvas show them the path. Within jeweled flowers, they are born through spontaneous transformation.
Receiving the Buddha’s prediction of enlightenment, they attain and realize immeasurable dharani-doors. All merits and virtues are fully accomplished.
Thereafter, they manifest countless bodies that pervade the lands of the ten directions. In a single thought-moment, they make offerings to all Buddhas throughout the Dharma-realm. In one...
Within this mindfulness, manifesting various supernatural powers, I deliver all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm and bring them to the realization of Equal and Perfect Enlightenment.
Even if empty space should come to an end, my vows shall never cease. Having finished the repentance and the making of vows, I take refuge in and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
Namo bhagavate. Vipaśyino ruciravaiḍūryaprabhasya prabho. Abhyudgatasya tathāgatasya arhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya. Tadyathā. Oṃ.
Vikṣate, vikṣate, vikṣaṭe, svāhā. Praise to the Ocean Assembly of Bhaiṣajyaguru;
to the King of Blazing Radiance; may the Eight Great Bodhisattvas bestow auspiciousness; may the Seven Buddhas assist in proclaiming it.
May the sun and moon turn their radiance [upon us]; may our merit, longevity, and well-being be eternal.
Medicine Master Buddha, Medicine Master Buddha, Medicine Master Buddha who Eliminates Calamities and Extends Life.
Namo Medicine Master Buddha who Eliminates Calamities and Extends Life.

(As previously described, after reciting the Buddha’s verses and circumambulating the altar while mindful of the Buddha, kneel before the Buddha and chant the *Yishan Fayuanwen* [Yishan’s Vow Text] for dedication.
I take refuge in the Teachers of the Ten Directions, Who proclaim the pure and subtle Dharma;
And the Sangha of liberation through the three vehicles and four fruits— I pray that you grant your compassion and graciously accept me.

I, [Name], the disciple, have personally contravened true nature and entered erroneously into the current of delusion. Drifting and sinking along with birth and death, I have pursued forms and sounds with greedy attachment.
The ten entanglements and ten proclivities have accumulated to form the causes of outflow; the six sense faculties and six sense objects have falsely committed boundless transgressions.
Mired and circling in the sea of suffering, deeply submerged on the path of heterodoxy, I am attached to self and addicted to others, setting aside what is upright to uphold what is crooked.
I look up to the Three Jewels with compassion for all karmic obstructions accumulated over successive lifetimes and every transgression. With a single-minded heart, I offer this repentance.
I pray that the Benevolent One may rescue and uplift me, and that virtuous friends may guide me, so that I may emerge from the deep abyss of afflictions and reach the further shore of Bodhi.
In this life, may my foundations of merit, lifespan, and status each flourish and prosper; in future lives, may the seeds of wisdom and the sprouts of the spirit likewise be hoped for.
Zengxiu was born in the Central Kingdom and grew up under the guidance of an enlightened master. He left the household life with right faith and entered the Way in his youth.

His six sense faculties were keen and sharp, and his three karmic actions were pure and harmonious. Unstained by worldly conditions, he constantly cultivated the *brahmacarya*. Upholding the prohibitive precepts, he remained untainted by the dust of worldly karma;

strictly guarding his dignified deportment, he caused no harm even to the smallest flying insect. He did not encounter the eight difficulties and lacked none of the four conditions for practice. Prajñā...
With wisdom manifest before them, they do not regress from the bodhicitta. They cultivate the True Dharma and realize the Mahāyāna;

they open the gateway of practice for the six pāramitās and cross the ocean of kalpas of the three asaṃkhyeya aeons. They erect the banner of the Dharma everywhere and shatter the web of doubt in its many layers.
They subdue all māras and cause the Three Jewels to flourish, serving the Buddhas of the ten directions without ever growing weary.
One studies and trains in all dharma-gates, attaining complete mastery of them all. One extensively cultivates merit and wisdom to universally benefit beings as numerous as motes of dust.

Having attained the six supernormal powers and perfected the fruit of Buddhahood in a single lifetime, one thereafter does not abandon the dharma-realm but enters everywhere into the realm of worldly toil.

Contemplating the compassionate mind of Avalokiteśvara and practicing the ocean of vows of Samantabhadra, he manifests physical bodies according to the categories and forms of beings throughout other realms and this world, proclaiming the sublime Dharma.
Within the hells and the miserable destinies, and amidst the realm of hungry ghosts, he may emit great rays of light.
Illumination. Or, manifesting various supernatural transformations, may all who see my form, or even hear my name, give rise to the bodhicitta and forever escape the suffering of saṃsāra.
May the lands of fiery cauldrons and icy rivers be transformed into fragrant groves; may those who drink molten copper and eat iron be reborn in the Pure Land;
and may those with fur and horns, those burdened by debt and harboring resentment, all be freed from their bitterness and sorrow, so that they may all partake in [this bliss].

To bring benefit and happiness: in an age of pestilence, he manifests as medicinal herbs to cure chronic ailments; in times of famine, he transforms into rice and grain to relieve the poor and hungry.
There is nothing beneficial that he does not promote. Next, he directs his aspirations toward all those who have been his enemies or kin over successive lifetimes.
May all present kinsmen emerge from the turbulence of the four modes of birth and cast off the entanglements of love spanning ten thousand kalpas.

May they equally share with all sentient beings in the attainment of the Buddha-way. Though empty space may come to an end, my vow shall be inexhaustible; may the sentient and the non-sentient alike perfect the seed of omniscience.
The merit of this practice of establishing the altar and performing repentance is most sublime;
may all its boundless and supreme blessings be dedicated so that all sentient beings drowning in suffering may swiftly proceed to the buddha-field of Amitābha.
The above causes and conditions are the Buddhas of the three periods of time,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, and Avalokiteśvara,
who abide in the realm of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā— like space, resembling a lotus flower that does not cling to water.
With a pure mind, transcending all else, I bow my head in homage to the Unsurpassed Honored One.
I take refuge in the Buddha. May all sentient beings realize the Great Way and attain the unsurpassed mind of the Dharma.
Taking refuge in the Dharma, may all beings enter deeply into the treasury of the sutras, their wisdom as vast as the ocean.
Taking refuge in the Sangha, may all beings lead great assemblies, free from all obstacles.
Homage to the Holy Assembly.
